b200_agentx_dep.description: Data-parallel ranks with expert parallelism and a Simple CPU KV tier behind a consistent-hash vLLM Router: DEP8 for concurrency 64 to 192, TP4 x DP2 at 32 and TP2 x DP4 at 48 and 64.
b200_agentx_dep.label: AgentX DEP
b200_agentx_dep.runbook:
The data-parallel points of the B200 AgentX lane (`dsv4-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp` and its low-concurrency
companion, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4554](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4554)) serve the
0813 checkpoint with DSpark (six draft tokens) as one engine on one 8-GPU B200 node: DEP8 (TP1 x DP8) for
concurrency 64 to 192, TP4 x DP2 at 32 and TP2 x DP4 at 48 and 64, all with expert parallelism and the Simple
CPU KV tier. Each rank gets 241.5 GB of host memory (1932 GB across the node), so size it to the machine.
`--max-num-seqs` is per DP rank, and `--max-num-batched-tokens` is an 8192-token prefill budget plus seven
verification slots per sequence. The TP4 x DP2 and TP2 x DP4 points leave `VLLM_DSV4_MEGA_FP8_COMBINE` unset.
TP2 x DP4 was measured on a second pinned image, shown on those points.

The lane fronts the server with vLLM Router 0.1.14 (`--policy consistent_hash`, `--intra-node-data-parallel-size`
equal to the server's DP size, as on the router tab), plus `--request-timeout-secs 14400` so long agentic
requests outlive the default and `--disable-retries` so a failed request is not replayed. Clients send a stable
per-conversation `X-Session-ID` so the router keeps a conversation on the rank that holds its prefix.

Left out of the command: `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` (removed in vLLM v0.30.0,
[vllm#55353](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55353), so it had no effect), `--served-model-name`
(the builder replaces it with the checkpoint ID) and the router's Prometheus port. The throughput points in
InferenceX swap block verification for synthetic rejection at a committed acceptance length so every point is
measured at the same acceptance rate; the command does not set it.

b200_agentx_tp.description: TP8 on one 8-GPU B200 node with DSpark (six draft tokens), FlashInfer sparse MLA and a fixed 50 GiB KV cache per GPU; no host KV offload.
b200_agentx_tp.label: AgentX TP8
b200_agentx_tp.runbook:
The TP8 points of the B200 AgentX lane (`dsv4-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp` and its low-concurrency
companion, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4554](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4554)) serve the
0813 checkpoint with DSpark (six draft tokens) as one aggregated vLLM worker on one 8-GPU B200 node: TP8, no
expert parallelism, no host KV offload. Each GPU holds a fixed 50 GiB KV cache and `--max-num-seqs` equals the
concurrency.

Concurrency 4 is the low-latency variant: a 40 GiB KV cache, the `deep_select` sparse indexer top-k backend and
graph capture up to 16384 tokens. Concurrency 10 sets `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 32768` and
`--prefill-schedule-interval 64`, shards the indexer at 4096 rows (`indexer_tp_shard_min_rows`) and leaves
`VLLM_DSV4_MEGA_FP8_COMBINE` unset. Concurrency 4 and 10 were measured on a second pinned image, shown on
those points.

Left out of the command: the lane also exported `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`, which vLLM removed in
v0.30.0 ([vllm#55353](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55353)) in favour of the flag above, so it had
no effect on the image it ran on; and `--served-model-name`, which the builder replaces with the checkpoint ID.
The throughput points in InferenceX swap block verification for synthetic rejection at a committed
acceptance length so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate; the command does not set it.

mi355x_agentx_dpa.description: TP1 attention / DP8 with tensor-sharded experts, DSpark K6 and session-affine routing; monokernel disabled.
mi355x_agentx_dpa.label: AgentX DPA8 + TP experts
mi355x_agentx_dpa.runbook:
This is the DP-attention arm of the
[TP8 profile](#preset-mi355x_agentx_tp), using the same checkpoint, image,
runtime prerequisites and real-versus-synthetic verification distinction.
The source qualification blocker described there remains unresolved.
Runtime flags are TP1/DP8 with no expert-parallel flag: experts remain
tensor-sharded across the eight ranks. The source's matrix label TP8/EP1
describes the aggregate topology, not the attention TP argument.
Monokernel remains disabled (the image default); TP8-only monokernel
eligibility does not extend to this arm.

Each DP scheduler caps sequences at the listed client concurrency.
The measured prefill interval is `8`; the `16384` long-prefill threshold
exceeds the `8192` token budget and does not bind.

For exact source routing, replace the generic router companion with this
pinned setup in another shell on the engine's host/container network:

```bash
uv pip install vllm-router==0.1.14
vllm-router \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --worker-urls http://localhost:8100 \
  --intra-node-data-parallel-size 8 \
  --policy consistent_hash \
  --request-timeout-secs 14400 \
  --disable-retries
```

Clients connect to the router on port `8000`, retaining an `X-Session-ID`
across turns of each conversation. InferenceX maps correlation IDs to
this header; `AIPERF_HTTP_X_SESSION_ID_FROM_CORRELATION_ID=1` is a benchmark
client setting, not an engine environment variable.

mi355x_agentx_tp.description: Source reproduction: DSpark K6 and monokernel on eight MI355X GPUs; draft communication precision requires resolution.
mi355x_agentx_tp.label: AgentX TP8 + monokernel
mi355x_agentx_tp.runbook:
This opt-in profile serves [DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813)
on one 8× MI355X node. The monokernel is enabled only for the TP8 arm;
[vLLM #61482](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61482) added this
DSpark-compatible path. These presets do not change the generic defaults.

**Qualification blocked:** the source enables nondefault INT4 QuickReduce
for draft collectives too. For example, 32 active K6 requests produce at
least 192 draft rows, making the BF16 attention-output reduction eligible
for INT4 communication in the pinned image. This conflicts with
[InferenceX's draft-precision rule](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/67de4b34ee1419b2a31c0e7200964a6e78015be4/CONTRIBUTING.md#draft-model-precision).
These are faithful source profiles, pending a source correction and
qualifying validation; they are not a production recommendation. Real
target verification and passing GSM8K do not resolve that precision issue.

InferenceX installs `Pillow fastapi uvicorn` before engine startup. When
using the pinned image interactively, install these prerequisites inside
the container, then run the generated Python command in that container:

```bash
uv pip install Pillow fastapi uvicorn
```

The generated Docker launch does not perform this setup step; provide the
dependencies in its container before using that launch form.

The source pins the target and tokenizer revisions, but supplies no separate
DSpark draft revision. DSpark loads the native draft from the same model ID
through the image's default mixed FP8/MXFP4 handling; no draft dtype or
quantization override is added. INT4 QuickReduce is shared by eligible
standard-path target and draft collectives, rather than being target-only.
The KV cache is FP8. The image is recorded as a tag, without a source-pinned
digest. Keep inherited environment settings consistent with the preset.

The generated serving commands use real target verification. For the
**InferenceX throughput sweep only**, merge the following keys into their
speculative config, retaining DSpark K6 and probabilistic drafting:

```json
{"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.77}
```

`3.77` comes from the committed
[DeepSeek-V4-Pro thinking-on K6 golden curve](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/5ec3c995988e5d3632c1ff53e8ae39da3e799892/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/dsv4-pro-0813-dspark.yaml).
Synthetic acceptance is a measurement control; do not use it for production
or accuracy evaluation. The generic Bench command is a smoke benchmark,
not an AgentX replay; reproduce AgentX with the linked InferenceX harness.

The TP8 scheduler caps are twice the listed client concurrency for AgentX
fan-out. No host-memory offload is enabled. The source's obsolete
`VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=32768` has no effect in this image;
the presets retain the effective CLI default of `0` (semantic checkpoints).

Evidence: [sweep 40260921924, attempt 3](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40260921924/attempts/3)
for source head `882db2060239f4d849f8b1c93f3b8b192ad3637e` covers all twelve TP8/DPA
throughput points and two real-verification GSM8K evals. The current-head
[run 40626241537](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40626241537)
only reuses that sweep; its performance/eval matrices are skipped.
Its actual CI merge `f301906060dcfd3b63ac6f77a735698f731f65b1` and the cited
head produce identical native recipe expansion for this lane.
This documentation change does not rerun GPU inference or establish private
agentic accuracy evaluation.

gb200_agentx.runbook:
The GB200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-agg-mtp`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4281](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4281)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three speculative tokens, FlashInfer draft attention, local argmax reduction) and the CUTLASS MSA decode kernel as aggregated vLLM workers behind the Dynamo frontend's KV-aware router. This preset holds its TP4 points, one worker per 4-GPU tray; [AgentX TP8](#preset-gb200_agentx_tp8) holds the two-tray TP8 points.

- **GPU-resident points** keep the whole KV cache in HBM. Their CUDA graph sizes start at 1 and 2 so the drafter's decode steps also replay full graphs.
- **KV offload points** add a host-DRAM KV tier through `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with lazy offload: 181 GiB of pinned host memory per rank, 724 GiB per tray. Where `--max-num-seqs` is below the concurrency, requests beyond it wait in the scheduler queue.

**Running it under Dynamo.** The lane ran Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016`, installed in the pinned image with `pip install --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com ai-dynamo-runtime==1.6.0.dev20261016 ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261016`. Start etcd and NATS (JetStream on, 32 MB max payload) once:

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\njetstream {}\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
```

On each worker tray, export `ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379` and `NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222` along with the generated environment, and run the generated flags with `python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` in place of `vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4`. `dynamo.vllm` hands engine flags to vLLM's own parser, so the dotted `--attention_config.*` flags work as generated (the lane passed the same settings as one JSON `--attention-config`). It rejects vLLM's API-server flags, so leave out `--tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking_mode": "enabled"}'`, and add:

```bash
--dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --request-plane tcp \
  --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","topic":"kv-events","enable_kv_cache_events":true,"endpoint":"tcp://*:5200"}'
```

The Dynamo frontend then parses tool calls and reasoning. To keep thinking on, send `"thinking": true` at the top level of each request, as the lane's client did, or add `--dyn-default-thinking-mode enabled` to the worker command; a request's own `thinking` or `chat_template_kwargs` still overrides that default.

Then start the frontend:

```bash
export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222 DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp
export DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens DYN_TOKENIZER_CACHE_BYTES=8589934592 DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=60
python3 -m dynamo.frontend --trust-remote-code \
  --router-mode kv --router-kv-events --router-temperature 0 \
  --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400 --kv-cache-block-size 128
```

The KV router uses the workers' KV events to send each request to the worker holding its prefix, and session affinity keeps a conversation on that worker: send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` request header. This Dynamo build warns that `--router-temperature` is deprecated and will be removed in v1.7; newer builds take `router_temperature` in the default policy parameters of `--router-policy-config`.

The **Verified** badge for this GPU is recipe-wide. These presets cover the NVFP4 variant only; the GQA draft and TP8 all-reduce overrides also apply to the other variants on GB200, which were not qualified.

mi355x_agentx.runbook:
This opt-in MXFP4 profile follows [InferenceX #4418](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4418)
at `f10885621773d1f900b6b4d002ee37863e583af3`: the
[`agg-variants.yaml` SRT bundle](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/f10885621773d1f900b6b4d002ee37863e583af3/inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/minimaxm3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agg-variants.yaml)
for `minimaxm3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`. It serves
[`amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4) on one
MI355X node, text-only, with no expert parallelism, model offload or KV offload.
Both TP4 and TP2 use Model Runner V2; every point sets `max-num-seqs` to twice
its client concurrency. INT4 QuickReduce, FP8 KV/indexer caches, the 0.9 memory
fraction and the 128-token graph limit are specific to this workload.

TP4 enables the [pinned `df6603f` monokernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392/vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/spec.py).
It handles supported physical decode widths 1–16 with EAGLE3 K3; larger or
mixed steps fall back to ordinary decode. TP2 omits `--monokernel` because
this implementation requires TP4. The profile reproduces that image, not
later monokernel implementations or general MiniMax-M3 defaults.

[Source run 39890471932](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39890471932)
contains the twelve throughput points and their real-verification evals.
The audited head's bound serving configurations match that run's source.
[Reuse run 40416678647](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40416678647)
skipped the GPU matrices; it is not a fresh qualification. The earlier
[#2959 baseline](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34609443618/attempts/2)
does not qualify this image or monokernel. Performance is reported by
InferenceX; local recipe validation does not reproduce GPU performance.

Ordinary serving and accuracy evaluation retain real target verification.
Throughput reproduction alone adds the following keys to `--speculative-config`:

```json
{"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":2.78}
```

The [golden 2.78 acceptance length](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/f10885621773d1f900b6b4d002ee37863e583af3/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml)
is for the three-token GQA draft with thinking enabled. Synthetic rejection
bypasses real verification; never use it for users or accuracy evals.
AgentX's `AIPERF_APPLY_CHAT_TEMPLATE=true` and required `vllm:` metrics prefix
are benchmark-client settings, not server flags. The source's
`dram-utilization: 0.20` is orchestration metadata, not KV offload.

gb200_agentx_agg.runbook:
The GB200 aggregated AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm31flash-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-agg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4632](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4632)) serves the default checkpoint text-only, with one TP4 `dynamo.vllm` worker per 4-GPU tray behind the Dynamo frontend. Add trays to scale out: the KV router spreads conversations across them. At 16 sessions per tray (GPU-resident KV) the lane measured 29.3k tok/s/GPU at 402 tok/s/user.

**Image and versions.** The lane used an arm64 CUDA 13 build of the `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash` image (tag `minimax-m31-flash-arm64-cu134`); any build of that image family for GB200 will do. Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261023` was installed on top: `pip install --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com ai-dynamo-runtime==1.6.0.dev20261023 ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261023`.

**Tuning rules.**

- `--max-num-seqs` is about twice the sessions one worker serves: 32 up to 16 sessions, 64 at 32-40.
- **GPU-resident KV** (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`) is enough up to about 16 sessions per tray. Beyond that, multi-turn contexts outgrow HBM and evicted prefixes are recomputed.
- **Host-DRAM KV offload** adds `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with lazy offload. `cpu_bytes_to_use` is the budget for the whole worker, split across its four ranks: 360 GB pins 90 GB per rank. Size it from the host DRAM that is free after the engine processes are up. Lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` to 0.82 to leave room for the transfer buffers. `--kv-cache-metrics` exports KV residency metrics, which help with that sizing; it can be left out.
- The CUDA graph sizes go up to 8192 tokens, so prefill chunks of up to 8192 tokens also replay graphs. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` still allows larger mixed steps, which run piecewise.

**Running under Dynamo.** Start etcd and NATS (32 MB max payload) once:

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
```

On each tray, export `ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379` and `NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222` together with the generated environment and `DYN_TCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120`, `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_LIMIT=1024`, `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_WAITING_LIMIT=1024` and `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_REQUEST_QUEUE_LIMIT=2048`. Then run the generated flags with `python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --trust-remote-code` in place of `vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`. `dynamo.vllm` rejects vLLM's API-server flags, so leave out `--tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice` and add:

```bash
--dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","topic":"kv-events","enable_kv_cache_events":true,"endpoint":"tcp://*:5200"}'
```

Start the frontend:

```bash
export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222
export DYN_ROUTER_ACTIVE_REQUEST_EXPIRY_SECS=3600 DYN_TCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens
python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000 --router-mode kv --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400
```

`DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens` switches the frontend to the fastokens tokenizer backend that ships with Dynamo. With 100K+ token agentic prompts, the default tokenizer spends about 150 ms per request on the frontend (up to 600 ms at p90), all of it added to TTFT; fastokens takes about 1 ms.

The KV router uses the workers' KV events to send each request to the worker that holds its prefix. Session affinity keeps a conversation on that worker for up to four hours; send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` request header.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden DSpark acceptance length (4.04), so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler (`rejection_sample_method: block`), as in the command above.

gb200_agentx_pd.runbook:
The GB200 disaggregated AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm31flash-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4632](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4632)) serves the default checkpoint text-only with Dynamo and vLLM. Several prefill workers, each DEP4 on one 4-GPU tray, feed one decode worker that is DEP8 across two trays or DEP16 across four. KV moves from prefill to decode over NIXL (UCX over RDMA), and every rank contributes host DRAM to a shared Mooncake KV store, so a returning conversation's prefix is loaded from the store instead of recomputed. Both roles use expert parallelism with DeepGEMM MegaMoE, attention data parallelism, the V2 model runner and the seven-token DSpark draft on `FLASHINFER_TS`.

| Prefill workers (DEP4) | Decode | GPUs | Sessions | tok/s/GPU | tok/s/user | TTFT p90 | E2E latency p90 |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | DEP8 | 16 | 224 | 94.2k | 250 | 3.0 s | 12.2 s |
| 2 | DEP8 | 16 | 256 | 98.8k | 244 | 5.3 s | 15.7 s |
| 3 | DEP8 | 20 | 256 | 86.4k | 240 | 2.4 s | 12.1 s |
| 3 | DEP8 | 20 | 288 | 93.2k | 230 | 3.5 s | 13.3 s |
| 3 | DEP16 | 28 | 280 | 70.4k | 302 | 1.9 s | 9.4 s |
| 3 | DEP16 | 28 | 320 | 77.3k | 291 | 2.2 s | 10.0 s |
| 3 | DEP16 | 28 | 360 | 85.4k | 284 | 2.5 s | 10.6 s |
| 4 | DEP16 | 32 | 352 | 74.5k | 284 | 1.8 s | 9.9 s |

The preset renders one prefill worker and the decode worker. Run more prefill workers with the same command, one per tray.

**Image and versions.** The lane used an arm64 CUDA 13 build of the `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash` image (tag `minimax-m31-flash-arm64-cu134`), with Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261023` and Mooncake `mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13==0.3.13.post1` installed on every worker and on the Mooncake master host: `pip install --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com ai-dynamo-runtime==1.6.0.dev20261023 ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261023 mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13==0.3.13.post1`.

### Tuning rules

- **Prefill pool.** The prefill pool sets TTFT, so scale prefill workers with load. The lane's points kept TTFT p90 between 1.8 and 5.3 s with one DEP4 prefill tray per 85-128 concurrent agentic sessions (2 trays at 224-256 sessions, 3 at 256-360, 4 at 352). Two prefill trays per DEP8 decode give the most tokens per GPU; a third keeps TTFT p90 near 3.5 s up to 288 sessions. Add a prefill tray when TTFT p90 climbs while decode still has room.
- **DEP8 or DEP16 decode.** DEP8 gives the most tokens per GPU: 28-36 sessions per decode GPU at 230-250 tok/s/user. DEP16 halves the batch per rank and gives about 25% more tok/s/user (302 at 280 sessions) and holds E2E latency p90 near 10 s up to 360 sessions, at about 10-20% fewer tokens per GPU. `--max-num-seqs 64` per DP rank is a cap, not the operating point. The decode graph cap is `--max-num-seqs` x (1 + 7 draft tokens) = 512. `--watermark 0.05` keeps 5% of the decode KV cache free, so extra requests wait in the queue instead of preempting running ones. Keep decode `--max-num-batched-tokens` at 8192: a preempted request recomputes its context in chunks of that size.
- **Prefill batching.** `--long-prefill-token-threshold 4096` chunks long prompts into 4096-token pieces. Short prompts then share each step with them instead of waiting behind a 100K-token context, which lowers the TTFT tail. The recipe's 1P1D section above uses 8192. `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` bounds a prefill step. Prefill captures CUDA graphs up to 2048 tokens. Prefill runs at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, decode at 0.88.
- **Mooncake pool size.** `global_segment_size` is registered by every DP rank, prefill and decode alike, so a tray pins four times that value. The lane used 190 GB per rank (760 GB per tray), which lets three DEP4 prefill trays serve up to 288 sessions with DEP8 and 360 with DEP16; 210 GB per rank ran the prefill trays out of host memory. Size it as (host DRAM free per tray after the engines are up - headroom for NIXL and the 4 GB local buffers) / ranks per tray. The decode ranks only add capacity to the pool (`kv_consumer` with `enable_lookup: false` and `save_decode_cache: false`): the prefill workers write and read every block.
- **Routing.** The KV router (`--router-mode kv`) reads the prefill workers' KV events and sends each request to the worker that already holds its prefix. Session affinity (`--router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400`) keeps a conversation on that worker for up to four hours. Send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` header. The Mooncake store catches the prefixes that miss after a reroute.
- **Transport.** Cross-tray NIXL needs `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy` with `UCX_NET_DEVICES` set to the tray's RDMA ports. Without them, UCX can fall back to TCP and transfers stall. Point `UCX_MODULE_DIR` at the UCX bundled with the NIXL wheel (`nixl_cu13.libs/ucx` in the image's `dist-packages`). `kv_lease_duration: 120` holds a prefill's blocks for up to 120 s until decode reads them (the default is 30 s).
- **NUMA.** `--numa-bind` pins each rank to its GPU's NUMA node. Decode passes the tray's map, `--numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1`, explicitly.
- `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is the same as the lane's `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`. `--prefill-schedule-interval 1`, also set by the lane, is vLLM's default.

### Services

Start etcd, NATS and the Mooncake master once, on a host that runs no engine workers, together with the frontend. The engine trays' host DRAM then goes to the Mooncake pool.

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
mooncake_master --rpc_port=50051 \
  --default_kv_lease_ttl=60000 --eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.95 --eviction_ratio=0.10
```

Every worker reads the store configuration from the JSON file that `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` points to (export it with the rest of the environment):

```json
{"master_server_address": "<infra-host>:50051", "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
 "global_segment_size": "190GB", "local_buffer_size": "4GB", "protocol": "rdma",
 "device_name": "mlx5_0,mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3", "enable_offload": false}
```

### Workers

Export `ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379`, `NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222` and the generated environment on every tray, then run the generated `python3 -m dynamo.vllm` commands. Add `--served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --trust-remote-code --dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3` to both roles. `dynamo.vllm` rejects vLLM's API-server flags `--tool-call-parser` and `--enable-auto-tool-choice`. Multi-node DEP decode runs one process per tray with `--data-parallel-start-rank` set to 0, 4, 8 and so on, and a shared `--data-parallel-address` and `--data-parallel-rpc-port`. `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` lets every tray's Dynamo runtime register its own DP ranks with the frontend.

### Frontend


gb300_agentx_agg.runbook:
The GB300 aggregated AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm31flash-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-agg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4631](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4631)) serves the default checkpoint text-only, with one TP4 `dynamo.vllm` worker per 4-GPU tray behind the Dynamo frontend. Add trays to scale out: the KV router spreads conversations across them. The lane measured 29.4k tok/s/GPU at 417 tok/s/user with 16 sessions per tray (GPU-resident KV, `--max-num-seqs 32`), and 96.6k tok/s/GPU at 185 tok/s/user with 56 sessions per tray (host-DRAM KV offload, `--max-num-seqs 96`).

**Image and versions.** The lane used an arm64 CUDA 13 build of the `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash` image (tag `minimax-m31-flash-arm64-cu134`); any build of that image family for GB300 will do. Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261023` was installed on top: `pip install --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com ai-dynamo-runtime==1.6.0.dev20261023 ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261023`.

**Tuning rules.**

- `--max-num-seqs` is about twice the sessions one worker serves: 32 up to 16 sessions, 64 at 32-48, 96 at 56.
- **GPU-resident KV** (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`) is enough up to about 32 sessions per tray. Beyond that, multi-turn contexts outgrow HBM and evicted prefixes are recomputed.
- **Host-DRAM KV offload** adds `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with lazy offload (`VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`). `cpu_bytes_to_use` is the budget for the whole worker, split across its four ranks: 860 GB pins 215 GB per rank. Size it from the host DRAM that is free after the engine processes are up. Lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` to 0.86 to leave room for the transfer buffers.
- The CUDA graph sizes go up to 8192 tokens, so prefill chunks of up to 8192 tokens also replay graphs. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` still allows larger mixed steps, which run piecewise.

**Running under Dynamo.** Start etcd and NATS (32 MB max payload) once:

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
```

On each tray, export `ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379` and `NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222` together with the generated environment and `DYN_TCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120`, `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_LIMIT=1024`, `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_WAITING_LIMIT=1024` and `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_REQUEST_QUEUE_LIMIT=2048`. Then run the generated flags with `python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --trust-remote-code` in place of `vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`. `dynamo.vllm` rejects vLLM's API-server flags, so leave out `--tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice` and add:

```bash
--dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","topic":"kv-events","enable_kv_cache_events":true,"endpoint":"tcp://*:5200"}'
```

Start the frontend:

```bash
export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222
export DYN_ROUTER_ACTIVE_REQUEST_EXPIRY_SECS=3600 DYN_TCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens
python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000 --router-mode kv --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400
```

`DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens` switches the frontend to the fastokens tokenizer backend that ships with Dynamo. With 100K+ token agentic prompts, the default tokenizer spends about 150 ms per request on the frontend (up to 600 ms at p90), all of it added to TTFT; fastokens takes about 1 ms.

The KV router uses the workers' KV events to send each request to the worker that holds its prefix. Session affinity keeps a conversation on that worker for up to four hours; send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` request header.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden DSpark acceptance length (4.04), so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler (`rejection_sample_method: block`), as in the command above.

gb300_agentx_pd.runbook:
The GB300 disaggregated AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm31flash-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4631](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4631)) serves the default checkpoint text-only with Dynamo and vLLM. Six prefill workers, each DEP2 on two GPUs (two per 4-GPU tray, three trays), feed one decode worker that is DEP8 across two trays or DEP16 across four. KV moves from prefill to decode over NIXL (UCX over RDMA), and every rank contributes host DRAM to a shared Mooncake KV store, so a returning conversation's prefix is loaded from the store instead of recomputed. Both roles use expert parallelism with DeepGEMM MegaMoE, attention data parallelism, the V2 model runner and the seven-token DSpark draft on `FLASHINFER_TS`.

| Prefill workers (DEP2) | Decode | GPUs | Sessions | tok/s/GPU | tok/s/user | TTFT p90 | E2E latency p90 |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | DEP8 | 20 | 280 | 93.1k | 240 | 2.7 s | 12.2 s |
| 6 | DEP8 | 20 | 320 | 100.5k | 229 | 3.3 s | 13.8 s |
| 6 | DEP8 | 20 | 360 | 107.9k | 224 | 4.2 s | 15.9 s |
| 6 | DEP8 | 20 | 400 | 114.5k | 219 | 5.9 s | 18.4 s |
| 6 | DEP16 | 28 | 300 | 75.0k | 296 | 1.8 s | 9.3 s |
| 6 | DEP16 | 28 | 360 | 85.8k | 285 | 2.4 s | 10.3 s |

The preset renders one prefill worker and the decode worker. Run more prefill workers with the same command. Two workers share a tray on GPUs 0-1 and 2-3 (`--device-ids 0,1` and `--device-ids 2,3` on `dynamo.vllm`). Give each its own `--data-parallel-rpc-port`, `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT` and `--kv-events-config` endpoint port.

**Image and versions.** The lane used an arm64 CUDA 13 build of the `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash` image (tag `minimax-m31-flash-arm64-cu134`), with Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261023` and Mooncake `mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13==0.3.13.post1` installed on every worker and on the Mooncake master host: `pip install --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com ai-dynamo-runtime==1.6.0.dev20261023 ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261023 mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13==0.3.13.post1`.

### Tuning rules

- **Prefill pool.** The prefill pool sets TTFT, so scale prefill workers with load. The lane's points kept TTFT p90 between 1.8 and 5.9 s with one DEP2 prefill worker per 47-67 concurrent agentic sessions, so 93-133 sessions per prefill tray (six workers at 280-400 sessions). Add prefill workers when TTFT p90 climbs while decode still has room. Two DEP2 workers per tray give the router twice as many prefill targets as one DEP4 worker.
- **DEP8 or DEP16 decode.** DEP8 gives the most tokens per GPU: up to 50 sessions per decode GPU (400 sessions) at 219 tok/s/user. DEP16 halves the batch per rank and gives about 23% more tok/s/user (296 at 300 sessions, against 240 at 280 on DEP8) at about 19% fewer tokens per GPU, and keeps E2E latency p90 near 10 s up to 360 sessions. `--max-num-seqs 48` per DP rank is a cap, not the operating point. The decode graph cap is `--max-num-seqs` x (1 + 7 draft tokens) = 384. `--watermark 0.05` keeps 5% of the decode KV cache free, so extra requests wait in the queue instead of preempting running ones. Keep decode `--max-num-batched-tokens` at 8192: a preempted request recomputes its context in chunks of that size.
- **Prefill batching.** `--long-prefill-token-threshold 4096` chunks long prompts into 4096-token pieces. Short prompts then share each step with them instead of waiting behind a 100K-token context, which lowers the TTFT tail. The recipe's 1P1D section above uses 8192. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` bounds a prefill step. Prefill captures CUDA graphs up to 2048 tokens.
- **Mooncake pool size.** `global_segment_size` is registered by every DP rank, prefill and decode alike, so a tray pins four times that value. The lane used 180 GB per rank (720 GB per tray), which leaves 80-100 GiB of a GB300 tray's host DRAM free with the engines up; 200 GB per rank ran trays out of host memory. A larger pool raises the hit rate at high session counts: going from 160 to 180 GB per rank, with the services moved off the engine trays, lowered TTFT p90 by 0.4-0.8 s at 280-360 sessions. Size it as (host DRAM free per tray after the engines are up - headroom for NIXL and the 4 GB local buffers) / ranks per tray. The decode ranks also write the KV they generate into the store (`save_decode_cache: true`), so the next turn's prefill can load the previous answer instead of recomputing it.
- **Routing.** The KV router (`--router-mode kv`) reads the prefill workers' KV events and sends each request to the worker that already holds its prefix. Session affinity (`--router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400`) keeps a conversation on that worker for up to four hours. Send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` header. The Mooncake store catches the prefixes that miss after a reroute.
- **Transport.** Cross-tray NIXL needs `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy` with `UCX_NET_DEVICES` set to the tray's RDMA ports. Without them, UCX can fall back to TCP and transfers stall. Point `UCX_MODULE_DIR` at the UCX bundled with the NIXL wheel (`nixl_cu13.libs/ucx` in the image's `dist-packages`). `kv_lease_duration: 120` holds a prefill's blocks for up to 120 s until decode reads them (the default is 30 s). `VLLM_MAX_ASYNC_KV_ADMITS_PER_STEP=4` caps how many requests with finished KV loads decode admits per step.
- **NUMA.** `--numa-bind` pins each rank to its GPU's NUMA node. Decode passes the tray's map, `--numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1`, explicitly.
- `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is the same as the lane's `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`. `--prefill-schedule-interval 1`, also set by the lane, is vLLM's default.

### Services

Start etcd, NATS and the Mooncake master once, on a host that runs no engine workers, together with the frontend. The engine trays' host DRAM then goes to the Mooncake pool.

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
mooncake_master --rpc_port=50051 \
  --default_kv_lease_ttl=60000 --eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.95 --eviction_ratio=0.10
```

Every worker reads the store configuration from the JSON file that `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` points to (export it with the rest of the environment):

```json
{"master_server_address": "<infra-host>:50051", "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
 "global_segment_size": "180GB", "local_buffer_size": "4GB", "protocol": "rdma",
 "device_name": "mlx5_0,mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3", "enable_offload": false}
```

### Workers

Export `ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379`, `NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222` and the generated environment on every tray, then run the generated `python3 -m dynamo.vllm` commands. Add `--served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --trust-remote-code --dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3` to both roles. `dynamo.vllm` rejects vLLM's API-server flags `--tool-call-parser` and `--enable-auto-tool-choice`. Multi-node DEP decode runs one process per tray with `--data-parallel-start-rank` set to 0, 4, 8 and so on, and a shared `--data-parallel-address` and `--data-parallel-rpc-port`. `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` lets every tray's Dynamo runtime register its own DP ranks with the frontend.

### Frontend

```bash

export DYN_ROUTER_ACTIVE_REQUEST_EXPIRY_SECS=3600 DYN_TCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens
python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000 --router-mode kv --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400
```

`DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens` switches the frontend to the fastokens tokenizer backend that ships with Dynamo. With 100K+ token agentic prompts, the default tokenizer spends about 150 ms per request on the frontend (up to 600 ms at p90), all of it added to TTFT; fastokens takes about 1 ms.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden DSpark acceptance length (4.04), so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler (`rejection_sample_method: block`), as in the command above.

mi355x_agentx.runbook:
The MI355X AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/)
(`minimaxm31flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark`,
[SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4671](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4671)),
on the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint with `--max-num-seqs` at twice the concurrency
(c64 admits 128). Throughput runs replaced block verification with synthetic
rejection at the committed golden DSpark acceptance length (4.04 for seven
tokens, 2.88 for three); the commands above keep block verification.

- **Concurrency 1-8** run mono decode with an FP8 KV cache and no DBO: a decode
  step of up to 16 tokens runs each layer as one fused kernel, and prefill steps
  stay at 8192 tokens.
- **Concurrency 16 and 32** run seven-token DSpark with DBO and an NVFP4 KV cache
  at 0.85 memory utilization, leaving headroom for DBO prefill.
- **Concurrency 64** runs three-token DSpark with DBO at 0.90 and adds a host-DRAM
  KV tier through `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, so cached prefixes are not lost
  once the working set outgrows the GPU KV cache (14.6M tokens at 0.90).
  `cpu_bytes_to_use` (1,349 GB) is the budget for the whole engine.

passed all seven performance points and GSM8K at concurrency 8, 32 and 64 at
`a328b4435` (single run):

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 551.0 / 515.7 | 6,766 |
| 2 | 548.9 / 410.4 | 6,918 |
| 4 | 546.3 / 395.6 | 9,494 |
| 8 | 407.4 / 240.0 | 15,411 |
| 16 | 228.6 / 168.3 | 27,275 |
| 32 | 172.3 / 115.1 | 54,158 |
| 64 | 71.4 / 47.3 | 75,434 |

|---|---|---|---|
| P DP8/EP → D TP8 | 164.4 (c256, 100) | 82.8 (c128, 150) | 3.95 / 4.11 ms |
| P DP8/EP → D DP8/EP | 162.9 (c256, 104) | 84.8 (c256, 112) | 6.77 / 5.87 ms |
| P TP8 → D TP8 | 31.7 (c32, 229) | 15.8 (c16, 243) | 4.19 / 3.75 ms |

(vLLM `tests/evals/gsm8k`, through the proxy) 0.855–0.900, within noise
of colocated TP8 + DSpark (0.890 / 0.885). B200 per-GPU throughput is
~0.8x GB300 in the same layouts.

gb300_dcp8.description: Decode context parallelism shards the latent KV cache across the 8 ranks: ~8x KV capacity at a higher per-step latency. Works with DSpark.
gb300_dcp8.label: TP8 DCP8 (long context)
gb300_dcp8.runbook:
Measured on 2x GB300 (8 GPUs), NVFP4 revision 4359ec6, `--max-model-len 65536`.

| | TP8 | TP8 DCP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| KV cache, NVFP4 (no spec) | 3.60M tokens | 28.76M tokens |
| KV cache, FP8 (no spec) | 2.38M tokens | 18.88M tokens |
| GSM8K-200 (NVFP4, no spec / DSpark) | 0.970 / 0.965 | 0.975 / 0.970 |
| c1 TPOT p50, 32k input, DSpark | 4.02 ms | 5.44 ms |

On NVFP4, 28.76M tokens is room for ~27 concurrent 1M-token requests
(KV only; serving at 1M context is not validated, the recipe caps
`--max-model-len` at 262144). With DSpark the draft's per-block
admission bound costs some of that capacity (~0.69x of plain DCP8 at
64k context; it doesn't bind at `--max-num-seqs 128` below ~99k
average context).

DCP8 only pays off when KV capacity binds: at `--max-num-seqs 128`
and ≤60k input its TPOT is worse than TP8 at every load we measured.
On the final stack, TP8 DCP8 FP8 at 60k input / 1k output measured
c1 TTFT 4.73 s, c1 TPOT 12.50 ms and 204 output tok/s at c64; with
DSpark c1 TPOT is 6.16 ms (AL 2.81).

gb300_pcp8_dcp8.description: Prefill context parallelism splits each prompt across the 8 ranks: ~3x lower c1 TTFT than TP8 on long prompts, but the lowest throughput. Text-only for now.
gb300_pcp8_dcp8.label: TP1×PCP8×DCP8 + EP (lowest TTFT)
gb300_pcp8_dcp8.runbook:
Measured on 2x GB300 (8 GPUs), NVFP4 revision 4359ec6, DSpark, real-text
prompts, 1k output tokens, `--max-model-len 65536`, without
`--enable-expert-parallel`. The preset adds EP, as used by the PCP
prefill side of the P/D presets; it was not benchmarked in this layout.

| c1 TTFT p50 / TPOT p50 | 8k | 32k | 60k |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP1×PCP8×DCP8 + DSpark | 0.16 s / 8.75 ms | 0.54 s / 8.77 ms | 1.08 s / 9.35 ms |
| TP8 + DSpark | 0.45 s / 3.45 ms | 1.87 s / 4.02 ms | 3.65 s / 3.82 ms |

Under load (DSpark, p50 / p99 TTFT): 60k at ~0.1 req/s 3.30 / 5.91 s
(TP8: 3.70 / 7.28 s). Best throughput is 86.2 output tok/s/GPU at 8k
(c16, 47 tok/s/user), vs 178.3 for TP8 + DSpark. GSM8K-200 0.965–0.970
with DSpark, 0.980 without. KV capacity 24.48M tokens without spec.

PCP requires `--language-model-only` (text only) for now.

gb300_pd_agentic.description: No spec decoding, prefix caching on: DCP4 on the decode node gives 4x its KV capacity, so long multi-turn sessions keep their cache. Text only.
gb300_pd_agentic.label: Agentic: P PCP4×DCP4+EP → D TP4 DCP4
gb300_pd_agentic.runbook:
Measured 1P1D on 4+4 GB300 with `agentx-harness==1.0.7` on
`semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126-256k` (393 sessions, ISL mean
100.9k / max 255.8k, OSL p50 376), 900 s per point, NVFP4 4359ec6,
no spec decoding, prefix caching on, `--max-model-len 262144`.

| | KV tokens (D) | c16 out tok/s/GPU | c32 TTFT p50 | c32 out tok/s/GPU | c32 req/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P PCP4×DCP4 → D TP4 DCP4 | 7.81M | 57.6 | 0.72 s | 92.5 | 1.185 |
| P PCP4×DCP4 → D TP4 | 1.96M | 60.9 | 14.95 s | 78.3 | 0.939 |
| P DP4/EP → D TP4 | 1.96M | 61.0 | 12.66 s | 78.9 | 0.969 |
| P DP4/EP → D DP4/EP | 4 x 1.51M | 54.3 | 0.98 s | 89.7 | 1.155 |

At ~32 sessions D TP4 runs out of KV (local hit rate 17–33%) and TTFT
explodes; DCP4 on D fixes it. DCP4 decode costs 12–25% ITL, so at ≤16
sessions P PCP4×DCP4 → D TP4 is better (it is the "P PCP4×DCP4+EP → D
TP4" preset with spec decoding switched off). Everything is past the
knee at c64.

Route each session to the same DP rank on DP sides (our proxy set the
`X-data-parallel-rank` header): without it the hit rate drops 14–22
points and TTFT p99 is 2–3x worse. DSpark on a DCP decode node is not
supported yet.

b300_agentx_agg.description: TP8 + DCP8 on one B300 node with the Inferact DSpark draft (K7 at concurrency 1, K5 at 4-8, K3 at 12-28) and an embedded RDMA Mooncake DRAM store.
b300_agentx_agg.label: AgentX aggregated (Mooncake)
b300_agentx_agg.runbook:
The B300 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3-fp4-b300-vllm-agentic-dspark`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4381](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4381), pinned to [`809f704`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/tree/809f7045172ea5effde45cef7cbe02918f25f968/inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/b300-fp4-mtp)) serves the default `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` checkpoint (MXFP4 weights) on one 8-GPU B300 node with DSpark speculative decoding and an embedded Mooncake DRAM tier. It is a benchmark configuration; the settings in this preset are its production-useful parts. Draft length falls with concurrency (K7 at 1, K5 at 4-8, K3 at 12-28), and each point sets `--max-num-seqs` to twice the concurrency with CUDA graphs covering `(1 + K) x 1..max-num-seqs` tokens. Throughput runs use InferenceX's golden acceptance lengths for DSpark (3.84, 3.62 and 3.00 for K7, K5 and K3).

**Mooncake store.** The builder's **Mooncake** option renders the master and store config with a 100GB segment, which is the default. The lane gives each of the 8 TP ranks a 256GB `global_segment_size` and a 4GB `local_buffer_size`, 2,080 GiB of DRAM across the node in total, so raise the segment above the default only when the node has that much pinned memory to spare. The lane's master sets `--eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.95 --eviction_ratio=0.10`, matching the builder, and leaves the lease TTL at the Mooncake default. The store runs embedded over RDMA with `P2PHANDSHAKE` metadata. Pin `device_name` to one ACTIVE InfiniBand port driven by `mlx5_core`: this lane's ranks use a single rail because the rails are isolated from each other, so a port that is down or an EFA `rdmap*` device (no RC queue pairs) fails registration. An InfiniBand port addresses peers with GID index 0 (`MC_GID_INDEX=0`).

**Kept out of the preset.** `--disable-uvicorn-access-log`, `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` and the benchmark client variables are InferenceX harness or logging controls with no serving effect. `--moe-backend auto` is vLLM's default selection and is stated only to match the lane. gb300_agentx_pd.runbook:
The GB300 AgentX disaggregated lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4047](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4047), points refined in [#4373](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4373), [#4516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4516) and [#4638](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4638)) runs Dynamo + vLLM with several prefill and decode workers. Every worker is TP8 + DCP8 across two 4-GPU GB300 trays; prefill workers also use EP8 with MegaMoE, and decode workers use no expert parallelism. KV moves over NIXL, and all workers share an RDMA Mooncake store in host DRAM. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5`), Dynamo built from `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`, Mooncake `0.3.13.post1` from the image.

| Clients | Prefill workers | Decode workers | GPUs | Decode profile | Decode attention | Decode `--max-num-seqs` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| 16 | 1 | 3 | 32 | Specialized | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` | 12 |
| 24, 32 | 1 | 2 | 24 | Specialized | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` | 12 |
| 112, 128 | 2 | 4 | 48 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
| 128, 152 | 2 | 3 | 40 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
| 240 | 3 | 4 | 56 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
| 240, 264 | 3 | 3 | 48 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |

Each point renders one prefill worker and one decode worker; start the table's number of workers per role with the same commands, two trays each. Run every worker command on both of its trays with the same `--master-addr` (the first tray's address), `--nnodes 2` and `--node-rank 0` or `1`. Prefill workers always use `--max-num-seqs 32` and target and draft attention on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`.

**Specialized decode (16-32 clients).** The decode workers use the `latency_specialized` decode backend from the [GB300 low-latency preset](#preset-gb300_low_latency). Its requirements are listed there: V2 model runner, FULL decode CUDA graphs, BF16 convolution state with FP32 recurrent state, DSpark with at most 7 draft tokens, no pipeline or expert parallelism, and DCP of 1 or TP. Both roles pin `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`: left unset, NIXL P/D raises the DCP KV interleave to the KV block size after the specialized decode has read it, so its spec-verify causal mask uses the stale value. The prefill workers do not set `--additional-config`, because the backend rejects the expert parallelism they use.

**Regular decode (112-264 clients).** The decode workers run the target and the DSpark draft on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`, an FP8 MLA decode backend that plans its split-KV work on the device; it is never selected automatically, and prefill steps use the configured MLA prefill backend. These points cap decode at 128 sequences with ReplaySSM, so TTFT is not traded for ITL by a standing decode queue.

The preset turns **Spec decoding** off, because the toggle's generic `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark` K8 draft was not qualified and specialized decode allows at most 7 draft tokens, and **Tool calling** off: `python3 -m dynamo.vllm` parses the remaining arguments as vLLM engine arguments only, so the vLLM API-server flags `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--tool-call-parser` are rejected there. For tool calling and reasoning output, add `--dyn-tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-enable-structural-tag` to both roles. This preset's DCP8 pools do not combine with a DEP decode pool, which renders TP1 with `--decode-context-parallel-size 8` that vLLM rejects; the DEP16 decode lane is the [AgentX 3P1D DEP16 preset](#preset-gb300_agentx_pd_dep16).

The preset selects the distributed (embedded) Mooncake store on the **KV Offload** row, which wraps NIXL and the `MooncakeStoreConnector` in one `MultiConnector` on both roles; the preset sets the lane's connector options on it (recompute on a failed load, offload off). Documented here only: the worker counts, the lane's Mooncake master options and store sizing (the builder's Mooncake option shows its own defaults), and the frontend's router mode and session affinity (the builder renders round-robin).

### Services

Start etcd, NATS and a Mooncake master once:

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
mooncake_master --enable_http_metadata_server=true \
  --default_kv_lease_ttl=60000 --eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.95 --eviction_ratio=0.10
```

Every worker reads the Mooncake store configuration from the JSON file that `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` points to. The lane registered 160GB per rank:

```json
{"master_server_address": "<infra-host>:<master-port>", "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
 "global_segment_size": "160GB", "local_buffer_size": "4GB", "protocol": "rdma",
 "device_name": "<the tray's RDMA devices>", "mode": "embedded", "enable_offload": false}
```

### Frontend

```bash
export DYN_ROUTER_ACTIVE_REQUEST_EXPIRY_SECS=3600 DYN_TOKENIZER_CACHE_BYTES=8589934592 DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120
export DYN_DISABLE_OPENAI_STRICT_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=1
python3 -m dynamo.frontend --router-mode least-loaded --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 1
```

`DYN_DISABLE_OPENAI_STRICT_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=1` skips the frontend's preflight validation of tool parameter schemas marked `strict: true`. AgentX sends the conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-Id` request header.

gb300_agentx_pd_dep16.runbook:
The GB300 AgentX 3P1D lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dep16-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4516), refreshed in [#4638](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4638)) runs Dynamo + vLLM with three prefill workers and one decode worker at 256, 288 and 336 clients (40 GPUs), with the same configuration at every point. Each prefill worker is TP8 + EP8 across two 4-GPU GB300 trays, without DCP. The decode worker is DEP16 (`--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 16` with expert parallelism) across four trays and runs the target and the DSpark draft on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`; prefill stays on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`. Both roles use MegaMoE, `--max-num-seqs 32` (per data-parallel rank on decode) and online MXFP8 for selected target projections. KV moves over NIXL, and all workers share an RDMA Mooncake store in host DRAM. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5`), Dynamo built from `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`, Mooncake `0.3.13.post1` from the image.

Each point renders one prefill worker and the decode worker; start three prefill workers with the same command. Run each prefill worker on its two trays with the same `--master-addr` (the first tray's address), `--nnodes 2` and `--node-rank 0` or `1`, and the decode worker on each of its four trays with `--data-parallel-start-rank` 0, 4, 8 and 12 and the same `--data-parallel-address`. Set `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST` to the node's RDMA HCAs on every worker.

`KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` is an FP8 MLA decode backend that plans its split-KV work on the device; it is never selected automatically, and prefill steps use the configured MLA prefill backend.

The preset turns **Spec decoding** off, because the toggle's generic `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark` K8 draft was not qualified, and **Tool calling** off; for tool calling and reasoning output under Dynamo, add `--dyn-tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-enable-structural-tag` to both roles (`python3 -m dynamo.vllm` rejects the vLLM API-server flags `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--tool-call-parser`).

The preset selects the distributed (embedded) Mooncake store on the **KV Offload** row with the same connector options as the [AgentX xPyD preset](#preset-gb300_agentx_pd); the decode ranks only add capacity to the store (`kv_consumer` with `enable_lookup: false`). Documented here only: the three prefill workers, the lane's Mooncake master options and store sizing, `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST`, and the frontend's router mode and session affinity (the builder renders round-robin).

**Target quantization:** `--quantization-config` quantizes these target layers online to MXFP8: the KDA `in_proj_qkvgfab` and MLA `fused_qkv_a_g_proj` projections and the latent-MoE `routed_expert_up_proj`/`routed_expert_down_proj` projections on both roles, plus `o_proj` and the shared experts (`gate_up_proj`, `down_proj`) on decode. The DSpark draft is not quantized: vLLM builds the named draft from its own unquantized config, and the lane's logs show the online quantization pass only for the target layers.

### Services

Start etcd, NATS and a Mooncake master once, and give every worker the Mooncake store configuration through `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`, as for the [AgentX xPyD preset](#preset-gb300_agentx_pd). The store uses P2P handshake metadata, RDMA over the node's NICs, a 160GB global segment and a 4GB local buffer, with offload disabled.

gb300_low_latency.description: One aggregated engine on the latency_specialized decode backend with the DSpark draft: TP16/DCP16 over four trays at concurrency 1, TP8/DCP8 over two at 2-4.
gb300_low_latency.label: Low latency
gb300_low_latency.runbook:
The `latency_specialized` decode backend provides a CuTe-based implementation for low-concurrency Kimi-K3 serving on Blackwell. The configurations below serve the default [moonshotai/Kimi-K3](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) MXFP4 checkpoint with [Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark), using one aggregated engine across 4-GPU GB300 NVLink compute nodes and the native Python vLLM frontend.

The explicit opt-in is `--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'`; `auto` keeps the stock decode path in this image. The specialized path requires the V2 model runner, FULL decode CUDA graphs, and BF16 convolution state with FP32 recurrent state (`--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32`). Keep `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and the capture sizes together: the lists cover DSpark draft and verification shapes. Prefill and eager/piecewise steps still use the stock implementation. This recipe uses PP1, no expert parallelism, and at most seven draft tokens; do not combine it with `--enforce-eager`, ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM, or adaptive verification. See the pinned [backend requirements](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py).

Make the same target checkpoint available at the same local path on every node, and make `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` available through the mounted Hugging Face cache. Run the preset's commands inside the nightly image on every allocated node, with four visible GPUs, host networking, sufficient shared memory, and the devices and network access required by your NVLink/RDMA deployment. Use the reachable address of rank 0 for `MASTER_ADDR` on every node and a distinct `NODE_RANK` from `0` through `NODES - 1`. The lane served the checkpoint from a local path with `--served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3` and `--device-ids 0,1,2,3`; the builder serves the Hugging Face id.

mi355x_agentx.description: The lane's every-concurrency settings on one MI355X node, for any concurrency; the per-concurrency cells are the AgentX cells preset.
mi355x_agentx.label: AgentX TP8
mi355x_agentx.runbook:
The single-node MI355X TP8 AgentX configuration follows [InferenceX #4393](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4393): its [master entry](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/dee7824e8ca3810cc36fe668ed75a927183af41f/inferencex-e2e/configs/amd-master.yaml#L766) and [lane recipe](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/dee7824e8ca3810cc36fe668ed75a927183af41f/inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml) at `dee7824`. It serves text with tool-call and reasoning parsers, using DCP8/A2A at every point. There is no concurrency-2 point.

**In the command builder.** Settings the lane uses at every concurrency are part of the MI355X TP8 command: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'`, `--stream-interval 10`, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm`, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm` and `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`. Weights load with vLLM's default loader (the AMD profile's `--load-format auto`): with `fastsafetensors`, the lane's servers ran out of GPU memory while loading weights on its image. The lane's `--moe-backend auto` is vLLM's default selection, so the builder leaves that flag unset. Other AMD GPUs keep the general AMD profile.

- **Spec decoding** serves the lane's draft, the published [`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark), with its attention on `ROCM_AITER_MLA` ([vllm-project/vllm#55966](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55966)), FP8 KV, probabilistic drafting and block verification. Draft length is tuned per cell in the matrix below.
- **Target quantization** is set per cell in the **AgentX cells** preset: resident c1 passes no online quantization config, preserving the BF16 target weights required by specialized decode. Every other cell quantizes only the KDA `in_proj_qkvgfab` projections to FP8 per-channel. Routed experts retain their native MXFP4 weights. The DSpark draft remains BF16 with FP8 KV: vLLM builds the named draft from its own unquantized config, so removing c1's target quantization does not change the draft's dtype.
- **DCP8** (`--decode-context-parallel-size 8`, `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA`, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, `ROCM_AITER_FA` prefill, and the direct DCP ops off) is part of the **AgentX cells** preset; this preset serves without DCP.
- The **Simple** KV-offload option emits the connector the lane uses (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `kv_both`, `lazy_offload: false`).

**MoE environment.** The lane sets `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1`, as the AMD profile does, plus `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` and `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`. The SiTUv2 path does not read `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND`. `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1` makes the FlyDSL MoE down projection write its per-route outputs as MXFP8 (FP8 values with E8M0 scales) instead of BF16 before they are summed. It affects only the target's MoE layers; the DSpark draft's MLP is dense.

**QuickReduce.** The lane also enables INT4 QuickReduce (`VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4`) with `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB=16`, so only tensor-parallel all-reduces of 16 MiB or more use the INT4 codec. INT4 all-reduce is lossy, so it is not in the builder. The DSpark draft's all-reduces carry only its draft-step tokens (at most 600 tokens × 7,168 BF16 values, about 8.2 MiB, at concurrency 60), and its context projection has no all-reduce, so the 16 MiB floor keeps the draft out of the INT4 path in every lane cell.

The lane's ten per-concurrency cells, with DCP8, the lane's draft and the qualified image, are the [AgentX cells](#preset-mi355x_agentx_cells) preset.

mi355x_agentx_cells.description: The lane's ten per-concurrency cells on one MI355X node: TP8 with DCP8 and the DSpark draft, GPU-resident or with host KV offload.
mi355x_agentx_cells.label: AgentX cells
mi355x_agentx_cells.runbook:
The single-node MI355X TP8 AgentX configuration follows [InferenceX #4473](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4473): its [master entry](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/8737db4e8a1fae1f2e9cd03d04f2e03d6bf90145/inferencex-e2e/configs/amd-master.yaml#L766) and [lane recipe](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/8737db4e8a1fae1f2e9cd03d04f2e03d6bf90145/inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/kimik3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml) at `8737db4`. It serves text with tool-call and reasoning parsers, using DCP8/A2A at every point. There is no concurrency-2 point.

**Per-concurrency tuning.** The Point row renders the lane's ten cells. Every cell requests `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with breakable CUDA graphs disabled (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`); because Kimi-K3 has no `torch.compile` submodule, vLLM resolves that mode to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at load. The [AgentX TP8](#preset-mi355x_agentx) preset keeps the builder's general values for any concurrency.

Every cell adds `kda_prefill_backend: fused` in `--additional-config`. Only **resident c1** also sets `decode_backend: latency_specialized` and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. On the pinned image, this [MI355X specialized path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) requires TP8, V2, gfx950, no KV connector and BF16 target projections. It handles pure speculative-verification batches of at most eight rows (c1 with K7); other steps use the normal layers. These lane-specific settings stay out of generic MI355X defaults.

The `resident` profile keeps KV on GPU; `offload` uses `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with 224.875 GB of host DRAM per rank. `--max-num-seqs` is 2 at c4 in both profiles, then 6/10/16/24 at offload c10/c16/c24/c32. Resident c1 stays at 1; offload c48/c52/c60 stay at twice concurrency. These smaller c4–c32 batches target p90 interactivity and can trade off queueing, TTFT and end-to-end latency. Every cell captures every even CUDA-graph size from 2 through `max-num-seqs × (1 + draft tokens)`, except c1 whose maximum remains 16. Agentic benchmark runs replace block rejection with the golden acceptance length; synthetic acceptance is not suitable for serving or accuracy evaluation.

**Image.** This preset pins the builder and the commands below to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392` (vLLM `df6603f0`), the image qualified by #4393, reused by #4473 and carrying #60683. The compatibility limits above refer to this pinned runtime.

### Reproducing one lane cell

Run each cell in a fresh shell inside the pinned image. This real-verification form is for serving and accuracy evaluation; `PROFILE` distinguishes the two concurrency-4/DCP8 cells:

```bash
PROFILE=resident
CLIENTS=1
case "$PROFILE:$CLIENTS" in
  resident:1) K=7; BATCHED=16384; OFFLOAD=0 ;;
  resident:4) K=7; BATCHED=8192; OFFLOAD=0 ;;
  offload:4) K=5; BATCHED=8192; OFFLOAD=1 ;;
  offload:10|offload:16|offload:24|offload:32|offload:48|offload:52|offload:60) K=4; BATCHED=8192; OFFLOAD=1 ;;
  *) echo "PROFILE=$PROFILE CLIENTS=$CLIENTS is not a lane cell" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1
export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm
export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm
export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0
export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0
export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0
# Lossy INT4-quantized all-reduce for messages of 16 MiB or more: not in the builder.
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB=16
# 1.56 TB of weights from shared storage, and long agentic prefills.
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200
export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200
export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1
# Required on the qualification nodes' MEC firmware 38; fixed in firmware 177.
export HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1

GRAPH_MODE=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
MAX_SEQS=$((CLIENTS == 1 ? 1 : 2 * CLIENTS))
case "$CLIENTS" in
  4) MAX_SEQS=2 ;;
  10) MAX_SEQS=6 ;;
  16) MAX_SEQS=10 ;;
  24) MAX_SEQS=16 ;;
  32) MAX_SEQS=24 ;;
esac
MAX_CAPTURE=$(((CLIENTS == 1 ? 2 : MAX_SEQS) * (1 + K)))
COMPILATION="{\"mode\":3,\"cudagraph_mode\":\"$GRAPH_MODE\",\"max_cudagraph_capture_size\":$MAX_CAPTURE,\"custom_ops\":[\"+fused_rms_norm_gated\"],\"cudagraph_capture_sizes\":[$(seq -s, 2 2 "$MAX_CAPTURE")]}"

EXTRA=(--additional-config '{"kda_prefill_backend":"fused"}')
if [ "$PROFILE:$CLIENTS" = resident:1 ]; then
  export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
  EXTRA=(--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized","kda_prefill_backend":"fused"}')
else
  EXTRA+=(--quantization-config '{"targets":{"*in_proj_qkvgfab":"fp8_per_channel"}}')
fi
if [ "$K" -gt 0 ]; then
  EXTRA+=(--speculative-config "{\"model\":\"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":$K,\"method\":\"dspark\",\"attention_backend\":\"ROCM_AITER_MLA\",\"kv_cache_dtype\":\"fp8\",\"draft_sample_method\":\"probabilistic\",\"rejection_sample_method\":\"block\"}")
fi
if [ "$OFFLOAD" -eq 1 ]; then
  # The lane's node gives the connector 1799 GB of host DRAM (224875000000 bytes
  # per rank); size cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank to your host. The fixed hash seed
  # makes identical prefixes map to the same block keys on every rank.
  export PYTHONHASHSEED=42
  EXTRA+=(--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}')
fi
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-num-seqs "$MAX_SEQS" \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --stream-interval 10 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens "$BATCHED" \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config "$COMPILATION" \
  "${EXTRA[@]}"
```

Outside this preset, the generic builder's **Simple** option uses 220 GiB per rank and does not set `PYTHONHASHSEED`.

### Throughput measurement only (synthetic acceptance)

The lane's throughput runs replace block verification with synthetic acceptance, so every concurrency point is measured at InferenceX's golden acceptance length for this draft. Only the `--speculative-config` changes:

```bash
--speculative-config "{\"model\":\"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":$K,\"method\":\"dspark\",\"attention_backend\":\"ROCM_AITER_MLA\",\"kv_cache_dtype\":\"fp8\",\"draft_sample_method\":\"probabilistic\",\"rejection_sample_method\":\"synthetic\",\"synthetic_acceptance_length\":$AL}"
```

| Draft tokens | Golden acceptance length | Lane cells |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 7 | 3.84 | resident concurrency 1 and 4, DCP8 |
| 5 | 3.62 | offload concurrency 4, DCP8 |
| 4 | 3.36 | dcp8 concurrency 10, 16, 24, 32, 48, 52 and 60 |

These lengths come from [`kimik3_dspark_probabilistic_sample_method_block_rejection_sample_method.yaml`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/8737db4e8a1fae1f2e9cd03d04f2e03d6bf90145/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/kimik3_dspark_probabilistic_sample_method_block_rejection_sample_method.yaml): SPEED-Bench coding prompts with thinking on, measured on B300 for `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` with probabilistic drafting and block verification. They hold only for that draft at those draft lengths, not for `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`. Synthetic acceptance skips real verification: never use it to serve users or to evaluate accuracy.

### Evidence and limits

- InferenceX [run 40132624130](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40132624130) passed all ten performance jobs at source `684d891612596e4ed9dbdd2f402865e288214815`. These throughput measurements use synthetic acceptance. The selected matrix, image and fully bound lane configurations match `8737db4`; this is reused source-run evidence, not a rerun of that head.
- The run's ten accuracy jobs use real verification and cover nine distinct lane cells: offload c4 was not evaluated, and c60 has both vendor and lm-eval jobs. See the [accuracy collection](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40132624130/job/121058737731). Performance collection and comparison were skipped in this unofficial run; no across-the-board throughput or latency gain is claimed, and these results have not been reproduced locally for this recipe.
- Model policy (vLLM as the native engine, `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` as the agreed draft): [`MODELS.md`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/8737db4e8a1fae1f2e9cd03d04f2e03d6bf90145/inferencex-e2e/docs/MODELS.md).

b200_tp2_kv_offload.runbook:
Measured by NVIDIA on vLLM v0.32.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0`) on two B200 SXM 180 GB with a
942-request multi-turn agentic coding trace (about 64k mean input tokens, most prefix tokens
reused across turns, outputs capped at 12k tokens), replayed at fixed concurrency with real
MTP acceptance (mean acceptance length 3.2 to 3.3). Host: 512 GiB RAM and 200 GiB /dev/shm per
server for the 160 GiB offload tier.

| Concurrency | Output tok/s/GPU | Mean ITL | Mean TTFT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 936 | 8.7 ms | 0.70 s |

Further concurrencies and the comparison against this recipe's baseline command on the same
image and trace are being collected and will follow in a separate update.

The 48-sequence cap trades time to first token for inter-token latency at 64 clients; raise
`--max-num-seqs` if TTFT matters more than ITL for your traffic. The offload tier only helps
workloads that revisit long prefixes; drop the `--kv-offloading-*` flags for single-turn traffic.

TP stays inside the high-bandwidth intra-node NVLink domain; the inter-node link carries only DP coordination, no tensor traffic. E.g. 2× H200 nodes → TP8·DP2, 4× GB200/GB300 NVL4 trays → TP4·DP4.
data.name: multi_node_tp_dp

data.description: Tensor parallel within each node, pipeline parallel across nodes. TP stays inside the high-bandwidth intra-node NVLink/IB domain; PP is what crosses the slower cross-node link. Good fit for very large models (e.g. Kimi-K2 1T on 16×H800) where pure TP across nodes would bottleneck on inter-node bandwidth.
data.name: multi_node_tp_pp

data.description: Disaggregated prefill/decode cluster. Splits inference into separate prefill and decode workers communicating via NIXL KV cache transfer. Optimal for high-concurrency, low-latency production deployments. Each role can be a single-node or multi-node DP/TP/EP pool, with its own HTTP port, NIXL side-channel port, and DP coordinator.

dynamo.description: NVIDIA Dynamo frontend + dynamo.vllm workers. Workers discover each other through etcd (TCP request plane, no NATS) instead of fixed HTTP endpoints, and the frontend adds KV-aware / least-loaded routing. Same prefill/decode pools as the native vLLM router.

infra.command:
docker run -d --name dynamo-etcd --network host quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.21 \

  --advertise-client-urls http://$DYN_CONTROL_IP:2379
infra.description: Control plane — start once on $DYN_CONTROL_IP before any worker or the frontend.

data.description: Single-node DEP. Expert layers are shared across all GPUs via EP, dense layers run independently in DP groups. Best throughput for MoE models on 8-GPU single nodes. For MoE models only.
data.name: single_node_dep

companion.description: Routes client requests across the DP ranks of the single engine process. --intra-node-data-parallel-size must match the engine's --data-parallel-size; consistent_hash keeps a conversation pinned to the rank that already holds its prefix.
companion.label: vLLM Router

data.description: Single-node data-parallel attention with tensor-sharded experts (DPA+TP). Every GPU runs its own attention replica with a private KV cache, while the MoE expert weights are tensor-sharded across all local GPUs instead of replicated per replica. Aggregate KV cache capacity scales with the GPU count, so long multi-turn conversations stay resident instead of being evicted and re-prefilled. A vllm-router in front spreads requests across the DP ranks. For MoE models only.
data.name: single_node_dpa_tp

data.description: Single-node TEP. TP splits dense layers and EP splits expert layers across local GPUs. TP must be set to GPU count to avoid OOM from replicated dense layers. For MoE models only.
data.name: single_node_tep

data.description: Single-node tensor parallel. Splits the model across all local GPUs. TP size is set to the GPU count at deploy time. The simplest multi-GPU strategy — works for all model architectures.
data.name: single_node_tp

companion.command:
# --port must match "lmcache.mp.port" in --kv-transfer-config.
# Size --l1-size-gb to ~75% of the host DRAM you can dedicate — pinned
# memory is unswappable; the pool grows lazily from --l1-init-size-gb.
# --max-gpu-workers 1 avoids concurrent-GPU-transfer stalls under heavy
# async-load pressure; CPU-side workers stay at 8.
lmcache server \
  --port 5555 \
  --http-port 8080 \
  --l1-size-gb 512 \
  --l1-init-size-gb 20 \
  --max-gpu-workers 1 \
  --max-cpu-workers 8 \
  --chunk-size 1024 \
  --l1-align-bytes 16384 \
  --eviction-trigger-watermark 0.85 \
  --eviction-ratio 0.10 \
  --eviction-policy LRU \
  --supported-transfer-mode lmcache_driven
companion.description: Run on the same node in a separate terminal, before vllm serve — owns the shared CPU-DRAM KV pool.
companion.label: LMCache Server

lmcache.description: Offload KV cache to a shared CPU-DRAM pool via LMCacheMPConnector — prefix caching beyond GPU KV capacity, one pool per node (not per-rank segments). Adds an LMCache Server tab; run it in a separate terminal before vllm serve.

offloading_cpu.description: Single CPU DRAM tier, under LRU eviction. cpu_bytes_to_use is the total across all workers — not per rank, as Simple's knob is — and should exceed the aggregate GPU KV cache, or the CPU tier just mirrors what the GPU already holds.
offloading_cpu.label: CPU

offloading_fs.description: Adds a filesystem tier behind the CPU tier, so cached prefixes outlive DRAM capacity and survive a restart. The CPU tier becomes a smaller staging tier; the filesystem carries the capacity. Point root_dir at fast local NVMe, or at a shared mount to pool one cache across instances. Object-store (obj) and RDMA-peer (p2p) tiers configure the same way in secondary_tiers.
offloading_fs.label: CPU + Filesystem

simple.description: Offload KV cache to CPU DRAM on each serving node via SimpleCPUOffloadConnector — one flag, no extra infrastructure. ~220 GiB of host RAM used per GPU rank.
simple.label: Simple

offloading.description: vLLM's built-in OffloadingConnector extends the prefix cache beyond GPU memory: completed KV blocks are copied out by DMA alongside compute and promoted back on a hit. A CPU DRAM tier is always present and is the only tier with GPU access; optional secondary tiers sit behind it and stage their transfers through it. Pick the tiers below.
offloading.label: Offloading
offloading.tooltip: Offloading Connector — vLLM's built-in KV offload path: extends the prefix cache into host DRAM, optionally backed by further tiers. Composes with the selected strategy.
